events.title: Crusaders Storm Constantinople
events.description: Troops of the Fourth Crusade breached the defenses of Constantinople and began sacking the Byzantine capital. They looted churches, palaces and libraries over the following days.
events.significance: The sack deepened the split between the Latin West and the Orthodox East. It also weakened the Byzantine Empire, which never fully recovered.

events.title: Fort Sumter Is Attacked
events.description: Confederate forces opened fire on Fort Sumter in the harbor of Charleston, South Carolina. The Union garrison surrendered after a bombardment of about 34 hours.
events.significance: These shots marked the start of the American Civil War. The war lasted four years and ended slavery in the United States.

events.title: President Franklin D. Roosevelt Dies
events.description: Franklin D. Roosevelt died of a cerebral hemorrhage in Warm Springs, Georgia, at age 63, early in his fourth term. Vice President Harry S. Truman was sworn in as the 33rd president.
events.significance: Truman inherited the final months of World War II. He went on to make the decision to use atomic weapons and shaped the early Cold War.

events.title: Salk Polio Vaccine Declared Safe and Effective
events.description: Jonas Salk's polio vaccine was announced as safe and effective after a very large field trial. The news set off celebrations across the United States.
events.significance: Mass vaccination sharply reduced polio, a disease that had paralyzed thousands of children each year. It became a landmark in public health.

events.title: Yuri Gagarin Becomes the First Human in Space
events.description: Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin orbited the Earth once aboard Vostok 1. He then returned safely from the flight, which lasted under two hours.
events.significance: The flight opened the era of human spaceflight and intensified the Space Race. Russia now marks the date as Cosmonautics Day.
